title.narrative: Livelihood Improvement for Women and Youth, LIWAY 2, 2025-2029
Livelihood Improvement for women and youth, LIWAY 2, 2025-2029

description.narrative:
LIWAY 2 programme aims to contribute to sustainable poverty reduction and social stability in Addis Ababa and regional cities by increasing incomes through improved wage and self-employment opportunities, primarily for poor women, youth and IDP:s.
During the four-year period of extension, LIWAY II will create additional employment opportunities and income for 143,000 women and youth in regional cities and Addis Ababa. Target distribution per regions will be determined based on the unemployment status of the regional cities and intervention areas that will be assessed during the inception period. As such, the overall impact of LIWAY, including the first phase, will be 400,000 women and young people to find or sustained jobs.
LIWAY works in four interrelated market systems (Labour, Micro and Small Enterprises (MSE), Medium and Large Enterprises (MLE), and Skills. These were selected based on their relevance to the target group of poor women and youth, the opportunity for positive impact, and the feasibility of interventions. These four systems are interconnected and together contribute to structural transformation. While work in the labour system enables target group members to better access jobs that already exist, work in the MSE system offers options for coping strategies when jobs do not exist, while providing higher quality work for some and opportunities to graduate from poverty for those that create rapidly growing enterprises. Work in the MLE system focuses specifically on the future as people transition out of agriculture and informal employment both in modern industrial parks as the pluralistic medium and large enterprises that offer more jobs. Finally, the skills system supports the labour, MSE, and MLE systems by enabling more target group members to access relevant skills to find good job opportunities, to start and grow businesses, and to provide firms with the relevant skills they need to grow.

LIWAY 2-programmet syftar till att bidra till hållbar fattigdomsminskning och social stabilitet i Addis Abeba och regionala städer genom att öka inkomsterna genom förbättrade löne- och egenanställningsmöjligheter, främst för fattiga kvinnor, ungdomar och internflyktingar (IDP:s).
Under den femåriga förlängningsperioden kommer LIWAY II att skapa ytterligare sysselsättningsmöjligheter och inkomster för 143 000 kvinnor och ungdomar i regionala städer och Addis Abeba. Målfördelningen per regioner kommer att bestämmas baserat på arbetslöshetsstatusen i de regionala städerna och interventionsområdena som kommer att bedömas under inledningsperioden. Som sådan kommer den övergripande effekten av LIWAY, inklusive den första fasen, att vara att 400 000 kvinnor och ungdomar hittar eller behåller jobb.

The LIWAY 2 programme aims to contribute to sustainable poverty reduction and social stability in Addis Ababa and regional cities by increasing incomes through improved wage and self-employment opportunities, primarily for poor women, youth and IDP:s.
During the five-year period of extension, LIWAY II will create additional employment opportunities and income for 143,000 women and youth in regional cities and Addis Ababa. Target distribution per regions will be determined based on the unemployment status of the regional cities and intervention areas that will be assessed during the inception period. As such, the overall impact of LIWAY, including the first phase, will be 400,000 women and young people to find or sustained jobs.

Overall Results Summary of the LIWAY Programme Annual Progress Report 2025
The report primarily covers the Extended LIWAY reporting which relates to activities jointly financed by EKN and Sida incorporating results from ongoing programs from phase 1. The EKN funding and program activities extend untill June 2026.
The Livelihoods Improvement for Women and Youth (LIWAY) programme delivered good results in 2025, generating employment and income opportunities for 125,533 women and youth in Addis Ababa achieving 179% of the annual target and bringing the cumulative reach to 402,042 individuals (182% of the full Life of Intervention target).
Of the total cumulative reach:
-159,252 are direct beneficiaries from programme-supported interventions -242,790 reflect broader system-level outcomes, indicating substantial indirect impact
Notably, 2025 results were largely driven by system-level changes from mature interventions, signalling a shift from direct delivery to sustainable market transformation
Distribution of Results Across Market Systems Performance was driven by scaled interventions across four interlinked systems:
-MSE system: 43% of total jobs and income opportunities -Labour system: 20% -Skills system: 19% -MLE system: 18%
This distribution highlights the central role of enterprise development, supported by complementary labour matching, skills, and industrial systems.
Breakdown of 2025 achievements:
Wage employment (new jobs): 46,322 (132% of target) Self-employment (new): 23,385 (134% ) Maintained existing employment: 55,826 (319%) New enterprises established: 1,880 (63%), Businesses with improved models/services: 16,775 (149%) Access to finance facilitated: 1,394 women and youth (139%) Business and technical training delivered: 20,483 (243%)
The programme collaborated with over 183 market actors (37% public, 63% private) and successfully mobilised ETB 445.3 million in co-investment including ETB 75 million in 2025 alone, demonstrating strong ownership and crowding-in effects by partners.
At the systemic level, LIWAY advanced policy changes (national childcare standards and MSE policy improvements), strengthened market functions through digital job-matching, e-commerce, and non-collateralised lending, and influenced actor behaviour (financial institutions adopting data-driven models, private actors scaling proven solutions, and government embedding programme approaches).
Labour System Results Summary
The Labour System in the 2025 LIWAY Annual Progress Report achieved strong results in expanding wage and gig employment opportunities for women and youth through digital job-matching platforms and labour exchange infrastructure.
In 2025, it reached 23,189 women and youth, representing 69% of the annual projection, with young women achieving 12,059 placements (83% of target) and young men 9,480 (67%). Cumulative reach stands at 81,073 individuals, including 40,544 young women and 36,481 young men. Wage employment dominated outcomes.
The system improved business models for 23 private providers. Key platforms drove impact: Afriwork (Masero) , HaHuJobs connected 4,929, GoodayOn , and AlenHomes.Digital innovations including biometric verification, full-service models, and hybrid Tech-Plus-Touch support enhanced trust and inclusion.
Higher-order impacts included greater bargaining power for women workers and recognition of childcare as economic infrastructure. Systemic progress featured adoption of data-driven matching by platforms and institutionalisation of national childcare standards.
Challenges like digital exclusion were mitigated through hybrid models and partnerships with TVT providers. Overall, the Labour System demonstrated robust scaling of inclusive digital labour intermediation.
MSE System Results Summary
The MSE System delivered the largest share of LIWAY results in 2025, significantly boosting income generation, enterprise growth, and job retention for women and youth via digital marketing, e-commerce, PPP bazaars, business development services, and access to finance. The MSE System exemplified scalable, market-driven solutions that sustain livelihoods beyond direct support.
It reached 80,789 women and youth (313% of projection), with young women at 36,055 and young men at 22,397 . Cumulative reach hit 174,011 individuals comprising of 78,027 young women and 49,376 young men.
Maintained existing employment was the stood out substantially.
Access to Finance
In 2025, LIWAYs access to finance interventions disbursed support to 1,394 women and youth (cumulatively reaching 3,822 and mobilizing over ETB 265 million in total), primarily via innovative item-based digital loans and cash-flow non-collateralised models in partnership with institutions like Hijira Bank and RAYS MFI. These tools are successfully shifting financial institutions behavior toward inclusive, data-driven lending, benefiting women- and youth-led MSEs by reducing collateral barriers and integrating with digital platforms.
What works well is the combination of product innovation, BDS linkages, and advocacy; key learnings emphasize the need for extended timelines, hybrid support for literacy gaps, and sustained multi-stakeholder coordination to embed systemic change.
Business and technical training reached 7,393 women and youth and 28,371 cumulatively.
Interventions like operational space improvements, digital marketing, and non-collateralised lending shifted market practices toward inclusivity and data-driven approaches.
Higher-order impacts included enterprise formalization and crowding-in of private actors. Policy enhancements improved access to public spaces for small businesses.
Challenges such as taxation and inflation were addressed through advocacy and co-investment.
MLE System Results Summary
The MLE System focused on waste management, recycling, and circular economy interventions to support enterprise development, job creation, and environmental sustainability in medium and large enterprises. In 2025, it reached 15,052 women and youth, with young men at 8,826 and young women at 3,523. Cumulative reach stands at 70,639 individuals.
Self-employment (new) was the primary driver with 11,185 beneficiaries in 2025 particularly strong among young men. Maintained existing employment added 3,867 in 2025. Wage employment contributed 11,681 cumulatively . Adult men benefited notably with 6,800 cumulative reach.
Interventions enhanced productivity, profitability, and competitiveness of manufacturing firms through systemic improvements in products and processes. Higher-order impacts included environmental gains from circular economy models and secondary employment in recycling value chains. The system generated 18% of total programme jobs. Private sector actors adopted scalable business models with reduced reliance on grants.Multi-stakeholder dialogues aligned incentives for co-investment. Capacity building of implementing partners ensured sustainability. Linkages with financial institutions and buyers translated skills into market opportunities.
The MLE System demonstrated how targeted support in key sectors like waste management fosters inclusive green jobs and enterprise growth. Challenges in market access were mitigated through partnerships. Overall, it strengthened systemic functions for long-term economic and environmental resilience.
Skills System Results Summary
The Skills System strengthened workforce readiness and alignment between training and labour market demand while contributing to institutional reforms in Technical and Vocational Training (TVT) systems. In 2025, it reached 6,503 women and youth (92.9% of annual projection), with young women achieving 5,568 and young men 935. Cumulative reach totalled 76,319 individuals.
Interventions focused on quality improvements in trainers, curricula, and content development. Higher-order impacts included better institutional reforms within TVT systems and enhanced employability for target groups. The system accounted for 19% of total programme jobs. Partnerships with TVT providers embedded digital literacy and market-responsive skills. National policy processes advanced through evidence-based advocacy. Hybrid training models ensured inclusion of low-literacy and marginalized groups. The Skills System facilitated smoother transitions from learning to earning. Challenges in skills mismatches were addressed through labour market alignment.
Overall, it positioned skills as a foundational pillar for sustainable inclusive employment. Systemic changes are embedding programme-supported approaches into national frameworks. The Skills System continues to build human capital for long-term economic opportunities.
Mobilised Resources from Impelementing Partners
In 2025, implementing partners and market actors in LIWAYs match-making/labour exchange interventions (digital platforms like Afriwork, GoodayOn, HaHuJobs, and Alen Homes) mobilised approximately ETB 27.2 million as part of the labour system total, with notable examples including Afriworks ETB 6.83 million revenue (reinvested in scaling) and Gooday Ons revenue growth supporting ETB 8 million in ecosystem income.
Cumulatively, these efforts contribute to the labour systems ETB 114.5 million leveraged and the programme-wide ETB 445.3 million in co-investments/in-kind contributions.
